items.texto: I remember instructions better when I read them than when I hear them.
I understand math topics better when I listen than when I see the information.
When instructions include many numbers, I prefer them written.
I prefer to hear instructions rather than read them.
I remember information better when I read it than when someone reads it to me.
When someone gives me instructions, I tend to repeat some details out loud so I do not forget them.
When instructions contain several numbers, I remember them better if I say them out loud.
If I write numbers after hearing them, I remember them longer, for example a phone number or a figure.
When instructions include numbers, I prefer them written rather than spoken.
When I get written instructions and someone also explains them out loud, I prefer to read them myself.
If I want to understand something, I prefer to talk about it rather than read about it.
If someone tells me some numbers, I do not need to write them down; I remember them just by listening.
I write information down to remember it and understand it better.
I understand numerical information better when I hear it than when I read it or do exercises.
I understand and remember numbers better (for example a phone number, an amount, a record) when I write the information.
When I do a task, I prefer someone to tell me the instructions rather than reading them myself.
I understand things better when I talk them over with others than when I read or write them.
I tend to speak out loud when I want to understand something related to numerical information.
I understand numerical information better when I see it and write it than when I only hear it.
I do things better when I rely on drawings, charts, or information I can see.
I enjoy hands-on work, for example drawing, wrapping, cutting, and similar tasks.
I feel comfortable asking a classmate for help when I need it.
I work better alone than on a team.
I feel better showing and explaining how something works than writing about it.
Working with other people makes me nervous.
If I have to report on work I did, I prefer to write it rather than say it.
I like working on a team because I feel I learn more.
I enjoy sports, crafts, or artistic activities.
I do a job better with written instructions than with spoken ones.
In a team meeting, I prefer to answer questions out loud rather than in writing.
My opinion is more important than other people's.
I tend to touch things to understand more about them.
I feel more comfortable speaking than writing about a topic.
I believe teamwork is important and useful, and I try to do it whenever possible.
I understand written assignments better than spoken ones.
I can help others better when I explain things out loud rather than in writing.
I really enjoy sharing what I know with other people.
When I want to learn something new, I prefer experiments, drawing, or a project more than reading or listening about it.
I work better when I do not have to listen to other people's opinions or views on a topic.
I prefer written tasks or reports rather than oral ones.
I prefer tasks I can do by myself.
I enjoy projects that involve drawing, building, assembling, or making things.
I prefer to answer questions in writing rather than out loud.
If I have to learn new and difficult things, I prefer to study in a group.
I prefer to make suggestions out loud rather than write them down.
